title: The Toll Booth Problem
question: What does NEAR (the network and its token) get paid per dollar that NEAR Intents settles, and where is that take rate heading?
hypothesis: Users pay a real toll to settle through NEAR Intents, but almost none of it reaches NEAR: the gas the network keeps per dollar settled will stay a tiny fraction of what users pay, as the flow keeps moving around the NEAR token rather than through it.

verdict.headline: FORECAST: the gas take rate is 0.0918 bps of settled value today and is forecast at 0.0808 bps in 365 days (eighty percent band 0.0152 bps to 0.430 bps, beyond the horizons the backtest can score); settled volume is 36,438,447 USD a day and is forecast at 41,347,553 USD in 365 days (band 22,774,231 USD to 75,068,181 USD); 93.1% of the volume touches no NEAR-chain asset today (forecast 98.9%).

sections.title: Executive claim
sections.markdown:
**Analysis**

NEAR Intents now settles about 36.4 million dollars of public flow a day [raw/forecast.json#/series/intents_usd/last30], and 93.1% of that value [raw/forecast.json#/series/no_near_share/last30] moves between assets that do not live on NEAR. The people who move it pay a real toll: over the last thirty days the measured user-paid spread was 59.4 cents for every hundred dollars settled [raw/forecast.json#/derived/toll_split/rows/2/centsPer100Usd/last30], and integrator app fees alone were 47.8 cents [raw/forecast.json#/derived/toll_split/rows/1/centsPer100Usd/last30] of it. NEAR's own cut, the gas its Intents contracts burn, was 0.0918 cents [raw/forecast.json#/derived/toll_split/rows/0/centsPer100Usd/last30] per hundred dollars: less than a fifth of one percent of what users pay to cross the booth.

The forecast says the gap stays open. A year out, the spread users pay is forecast at 64.5 cents per hundred dollars [raw/forecast.json#/derived/toll_split/rows/2/centsPer100Usd/plus365/central], while the gas NEAR keeps is forecast flat at 0.0808 cents [raw/forecast.json#/derived/toll_split/rows/0/centsPer100Usd/plus365/central]. Volume can keep growing and the network can keep shrinking as a consumer chain, and NEAR the token will still be paid almost nothing per dollar settled, unless the fee switch the protocol announced turns into a visible, growing flow back to NEAR. That is the toll booth problem, and it is the number to watch.

**Analysis**

- If NEAR's gas take rises above 0.187 cents per hundred dollars settled [raw/forecast.json#/series/take_rate_gas/checkpoints/0/band80/1] at the first checkpoint, the claim that NEAR's cut stays flat is wrong.
- If the share of settled value that touches no NEAR asset falls below 89.1% [raw/forecast.json#/series/no_near_share/horizons/0/band80/0] within ninety days, NEAR assets are being used again and the "booth for other chains" framing weakens.
- If the fee switch starts routing a visible and growing share of the toll to NEAR-aligned recipients (buybacks, the treasury, stakers), the problem is being solved and the thesis should be rewritten around how fast. sections.title: Methods
sections.markdown:
Each series is a daily series. The model works on the seven-day mean of the observed days (a day with no value is skipped, never counted as zero), on a transformed scale: ln(one plus x) for counts and amounts, the logit for shares, ln(x) for ratios such as the take rate.

Five candidate models: the last value (naive); a random walk with drift estimated on the trailing 180 days; a linear trend on the trailing 180 days; a damped trend (Holt, damping 0.900, smoothing parameters fitted by one-step squared error on a fixed grid); and the median of the last three. [raw/forecast.json#/method/config/trailing][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/phi]

Rolling-origin backtest: origins every 14 days from day 150 of the series; horizons 30, 60 and 90 days; the target is the thirty-day average ending at the horizon, scored by the absolute error of its transformed value. Skill is one minus the model error divided by the naive error. The model with the lowest error at 90 days is used for each series, the simpler model on a tie. [raw/forecast.json#/method/config/originStep][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/firstOrigin][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/horizons/0][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/horizons/1][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/horizons/2]

Bands: the fifty and eighty percent half-widths are the empirical quantiles of the chosen model's absolute backtest errors at each scored horizon; beyond 90 days they widen with the square root of the horizon ratio, which is an assumption because the data cannot score longer horizons. Calibration reports how often the eighty percent band held the realised value in a time-ordered check that sets the width from earlier origins only (the verdict uses it when it has at least six test points, otherwise leaving each origin out in turn). [raw/forecast.json#/method/config/horizons/2]

Simulation: 2,000 paths from a block bootstrap (block length 14 days) of the chosen model's one-step residuals, with seeds derived from the input hash c8f448d8d5f2. The crossover and the twelve-month totals are read from these paths. [raw/forecast.json#/method/config/paths][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/block][raw/forecast.json#/inputHash]

Verdict per series: FORECAST_WITH_SKILL when the model beats naive by at least 10% at 90 days and the eighty percent band is calibrated between 65% and 95%; otherwise FORECAST_LOW_SKILL. A model that cannot beat naive is reported as such and naive is used with its wider bands. [raw/forecast.json#/method/config/skillThreshold][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/horizons/2][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/calibrationRange/0][raw/forecast.json#/method/config/calibrationRange/1]

Series definitions, quoted from the manifest:

- F2 tail_tx and F3 tail_signers: the long tail of ordinary accounts: Per signer and day, organic transactions n_org = all transactions minus those addressed to the Intents verifier contracts and minus bridge/omni receivers. The head is every signer with n_org >= 100 that day; the tail is every signer with 0 < n_org < 100. tail_tx = sum of n_org over tail signers (organic transactions of accounts outside the heavy head); tail_signers = number of such signers. OVERLAP ANSWER: tail_tx does NOT contain Intents or bridge transactions, because those are removed before the head/tail split (tx_organic = tail_tx + head organic transactions exactly, checked on every day below). F2 therefore does not overlap F1 in transactions. The same accounts can appear in both series as signers (an account can sign an organic transaction and an Intents transaction on the same day); a signer with only Intents transactions on a day (n_org = 0) is in neither tail_signers nor the head. [raw/manifest.json#/datasets/1/title][raw/manifest.json#/datasets/1/definition]
- F1 intents_tx: transactions per day addressed to the Intents contracts: Transactions of the day whose receiver_account_id is one of intents.near, verifier2.near (the Intents verifier contracts; account rule version 1, services/ingestion/src/backfill/account-sql.ts), counted over ALL signers (head and tail). Bridge and omni-token receivers (bridge.near, omft.near, v2_1.omni.hot.tg and *.omft.near) are a separate class (tx_bridge) and are not in this count. A transaction is counted once, by its receiver. [raw/manifest.json#/datasets/0/title][raw/manifest.json#/datasets/0/definition]
- F4 intents_usd: USD volume of successful Intents swaps per day: Sum of amount_in_usd (the provider's USD value of the input amount, exact Decimal(76,18) sum) over swaps with status SUCCESS and a known USD value, by created_day (UTC): the research definition. A day with a SUCCESS swap whose USD is NULL would be null (none is in this window). Days whose swaps are marked partial in source_coverage (provider near-explorer, dataset intents_swaps: 2025-11-09 oldest edge, 2026-01-27/28/30 quarantined pages, 2026-04-02 to 2026-04-23 explorer cursor jump, 2026-07-23 quarantined page) are left out of this series entirely, and so are the two days (2026-02-02 and 2026-02-04) on which a successful swap has no USD value (the day is incomplete by the research definition); they are listed as missing days and never filled with zero or estimated. [raw/manifest.json#/datasets/4/title][raw/manifest.json#/datasets/4/definition]
- What moves through Intents: stable-to-stable, no-NEAR-asset and NEAR-token shares of daily USD volume: Volume = successful swaps with a known USD value (the F4 definition), per created_day (UTC). Each swap leg (origin_asset, destination_asset) is joined to nearesis_live.asset_registry on provider_asset_id. F5 stable_share: both legs are a stablecoin, by upper-cased registry symbol_observed in {DAI, FRAX, USD1, USDC, USDCX, USDG, USDT, USDT0, USDe, USDf} (the frozen research snapshot's stablecoinSet; USDT0 and USDCx variants count, a deprecated-suffix symbol does not). F6 no_near_share: both legs mapped and NEITHER leg has registry blockchain 'near' (a stablecoin or token issued on NEAR counts as a NEAR-chain asset). F7 near_token_share: either leg has symbol NEAR or wNEAR (asset ids listed in asset_sets: nep141:wrap.near is wNEAR on NEAR; the NEAR token on BNB chain is also listed; F6 and F7 can overlap only for that BNB-chain leg). unknown_share: a swap with an unmapped leg (no registry row) is counted in unknown_usd only, never in F5, F6 or F7; shares divide by total_usd including unknown. The registry rows are used regardless of valid_from: every row has valid_from 2026-05-01 (the registry load stamp, valid_to is null everywhere), and applying it as a validity start would wrongly unmap every swap before that date. Shares are the share of the day's USD volume, not of swap counts. Days whose swaps are marked partial in source_coverage (provider near-explorer, dataset intents_swaps: 2025-11-09 oldest edge, 2026-01-27/28/30 quarantined pages, 2026-04-02 to 2026-04-23 explorer cursor jump, 2026-07-23 quarantined page) are left out of this series entirely, and so are the two days (2026-02-02 and 2026-02-04) on which a successful swap has no USD value (the day is incomplete by the research definition); they are listed as missing days and never filled with zero or estimated. [raw/manifest.json#/datasets/6/title][raw/manifest.json#/datasets/6/definition]
- New organic signers per day (first organic day seen since the window start): Organic signers (any size, tail and head) whose first organic transaction since the window start (2025-11-10) falls on that day. "New" means first seen SINCE 2025-11-10, not lifetime first-seen, so early days include returning accounts that had been inactive; the window-start day itself (every signer is new by construction) is left out and listed as a missing day. Head signers are a negligible share of the count (see head_accounts_break), so this is read as new long-tail signers. [raw/manifest.json#/datasets/3/title][raw/manifest.json#/datasets/3/definition]
- Head accounts around 2026-04-02: transactions in the 31 days before and after: The 12 head accounts (organic transactions >= 100 on a day) with the largest of their before and after totals. Before = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-01 and after = 2026-04-02 to 2026-05-02, 31 days each. tx_* sums organic transactions on the days the account was in the head; avg_daily_* = that sum divided by 31. On a day below 100 organic transactions the account is not stored, so the averages are lower bounds for accounts that were in the head on fewer days than 31 (head_days_* says how many). [raw/manifest.json#/datasets/10/title][raw/manifest.json#/datasets/10/definition]

Overlap of the Intents and long-tail series: tail_tx does NOT contain Intents or bridge transactions, because those are removed before the head/tail split (tx_organic = tail_tx + head organic transactions exactly, checked on every day below). F2 therefore does not overlap F1 in transactions. [raw/manifest.json#/datasets/1/definition]

Fee inputs: Per UTC block day: the sum of tokens_burnt (yoctoNEAR, and the same in NEAR = yocto / 10^24) and gas_burnt over every row of execution_outcomes (transaction outcomes and receipt outcomes, incl. refund receipts that burn no tokens), the outcome count, and the day's mean gas price = sum of blocks.gas_price / block count. Gross tokens_burnt of the outcomes. Whether part of a fee is burnt or paid to the called contract: nearcore docs state a 30% contract reward up to protocol version 86 and 0% from 87 (docs/economics/SEMANTICS.md); the mainnet activation date of version 87 is not verified here, so no burnt/paid split is applied. [raw/fees/manifest.json#/datasets/0/definition]

sections.title: Evidence against
sections.markdown:
**Analysis**

- The forecasts are uncertain. In the time-ordered backtest only 50.0% [raw/forecast.json#/series/intents_tx/calibration/pooledForward80] of realised Intents transaction values fell inside the eighty percent band, so the bands are too narrow and every series is labelled low skill. The gas take rate itself shows a skill of 0 [raw/forecast.json#/series/take_rate_gas/skill90] over a naive forecast: its central path is simply the latest level held flat.
- Gas is only one toll. The protocol's fee switch sends part of the front-end and protocol fees to NEAR buybacks, and our swap data sees that flow only partly (raw/fees/FEE_MODEL.md). If most of it travels outside the public records, NEAR's real cut is larger than this thesis measures.
- A small rate on a large base is still money: the forecast twelve-month gas burn by the Intents contracts is 33.2 thousand NEAR [raw/forecast.json#/derived/intents_burn_near_12m/centralTotal], about 113 thousand dollars [raw/forecast.json#/derived/intents_burn_near_12m/usdAtLastClose/central] at the last close, with the price held fixed. Whether that is "almost nothing" depends on what NEAR needs to earn.
- Volume is the least predictable input: a year out, the eighty percent band for daily settled value runs from 22.8 million [raw/forecast.json#/series/intents_usd/horizons/2/band80/0] to 75.1 million dollars [raw/forecast.json#/series/intents_usd/horizons/2/band80/1].
- Part of the flow is now private and invisible to us, and every figure here describes the public flow only.

**Computed**

- Gas is only one toll. Protocol fees, app fees and referral fees may reach NEAR-aligned parties in ways this thesis cannot see; it measures NEAR burnt as gas and the user-paid spread, and nothing else.
- A low take rate with large volume can still be the larger number in absolute terms: the twelve-month NEAR burnt by the Intents contracts is 33,183 NEAR on the central path, worth 113,476 USD at the last close. sections.title: Long-term economic mechanisms
sections.markdown:
**Analysis**

Interpretation. A booth that charges almost nothing can be a moat: if NEAR is the cheapest place to settle cross-chain intents, volume concentrates there, and a later, modest fee could be worth more than a high fee today. It can also be a leak: wallets and apps on top collect the toll, solvers collect the spread, and the network that provides finality is reduced to a utility whose token is optional for every swap. The fee switch is the hinge between the two readings. The thesis does not claim which one wins; it claims that, on the evidence so far, the value is flowing around the token rather than through it, and it names the checkpoints at which that will be visible either way.

**Computed**

- NEAR is paid when a transaction burns gas: a share of the gas fee is burnt, so the Intents contracts pay NEAR in proportion to the transactions addressed to them, not in proportion to the dollars those transactions settle. A larger settled size per transaction therefore lowers the take rate, and more transactions of the same size raise the NEAR burnt without changing the rate.
- The user-paid spread (the gap between the quoted and the executed price) is paid to market makers and the protocol's solver network; it reaches NEAR only if the receiving parties are NEAR-aligned, which this thesis cannot observe.
- Stablecoin movement between other chains pays the same gas as any other swap but carries little price risk for the user, so a rising stable-to-stable share can lower the take rate without lowering the activity.
- These mechanisms are stated as hypotheses to be checked by the checkpoints, not as findings.

sections.title: Reproduction
sections.markdown:
From the repository root `nearesis-app`:
- `pnpm thesis:data` re-freezes thesis/raw from the local databases (read-only SELECTs); add `--bigquery` to re-run the billed BigQuery cross-checks.
- `pnpm thesis:build` runs the forecast engine on the frozen data and writes raw/forecast.json, THESIS.md, FACTS.md, the static site, thesis.json and HASHES.json, offline.
- `pnpm thesis:verify` rebuilds into a temporary directory and compares every hash, including raw/forecast.json; it exits with an error if any file differs.
- `pnpm thesis:verify --dir thesis/archive/intents-vs-price-v1` verifies the archived previous version.
Input hashes are listed in the Source index; output hashes are in thesis/build/HASHES.json.

    t.receiver_account_id IN ('intents.near', 'verifier2.near') AS is_intents,
    GREATEST(CAST(t.receiver_account_id IN ('bridge.near', 'omft.near', 'v2_1.omni.hot.tg') AS INT64), CAST(ENDS_WITH(t.receiver_account_id, '.omft.near') AS INT64)) = 1 AS is_bridge
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.crypto_near_mainnet_us.transactions` t
  WHERE t.block_date >= start_date AND t.block_date < end_date
), s AS (
  SELECT block_date, signer, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNTIF(is_intents) AS n_int, COUNTIF(is_bridge AND NOT is_intents) AS n_br
  FROM tx GROUP BY block_date, signer

  SELECT block_date, signer, n, n_int, n_br, n - n_int - n_br AS n_org FROM s

  FROM ranked GROUP BY block_date

  COALESCE(org.head_tx, 0) AS head_tx, COALESCE(org.top10_tx, 0) AS top10_tx
FROM tot LEFT JOIN org ON org.block_date = tot.block_date

tables.name: intents_tx_daily
tables.purpose: Transactions of the day whose receiver_account_id is one of intents.near, verifier2.near (the Intents verifier contracts; account rule version 1, services/ingestion/src/backfill/account-sql.ts), counted over ALL signers (head and tail). Bridge and omni-token receivers (bridge.near, omft.near, v2_1.omni.hot.tg and *.omft.near) are a separate class (tx_bridge) and are not in this count. A transaction is counted once, by its receiver.

tables.name: tail_daily
tables.purpose: Per signer and day, organic transactions n_org = all transactions minus those addressed to the Intents verifier contracts and minus bridge/omni receivers. The head is every signer with n_org >= 100 that day; the tail is every signer with 0 < n_org < 100. tail_tx = sum of n_org over tail signers (organic transactions of accounts outside the heavy head); tail_signers = number of such signers. OVERLAP ANSWER: tail_tx does NOT contain Intents or bridge transactions, because those are removed before the head/tail split (tx_organic = tail_tx + head organic transactions exactly, checked on every day below). F2 therefore does not overlap F1 in transactions. The same accounts can appear in both series as signers (an account can sign an organic transaction and an Intents transaction on the same day); a signer with only Intents transactions on a day (n_org = 0) is in neither tail_signers nor the head.

tables.name: transactions_daily
tables.purpose: tx_total = every row of the transactions table for the block_date; signers_total = distinct signers; tx_organic / signers_organic = the same after removing Intents-verifier and bridge/omni receivers; tx_head = organic transactions of signers with n_org >= 100 that day (sum over account_daily_head); tx_top10 = organic transactions of the 10 organic signers with the most organic transactions that day.

tables.name: new_signers_daily
tables.purpose: Organic signers (any size, tail and head) whose first organic transaction since the window start (2025-11-10) falls on that day. "New" means first seen SINCE 2025-11-10, not lifetime first-seen, so early days include returning accounts that had been inactive; the window-start day itself (every signer is new by construction) is left out and listed as a missing day. Head signers are a negligible share of the count (see head_accounts_break), so this is read as new long-tail signers.

tables.name: intents_volume_daily
tables.purpose: Sum of amount_in_usd (the provider's USD value of the input amount, exact Decimal(76,18) sum) over swaps with status SUCCESS and a known USD value, by created_day (UTC): the research definition. A day with a SUCCESS swap whose USD is NULL would be null (none is in this window). Days whose swaps are marked partial in source_coverage (provider near-explorer, dataset intents_swaps: 2025-11-09 oldest edge, 2026-01-27/28/30 quarantined pages, 2026-04-02 to 2026-04-23 explorer cursor jump, 2026-07-23 quarantined page) are left out of this series entirely, and so are the two days (2026-02-02 and 2026-02-04) on which a successful swap has no USD value (the day is incomplete by the research definition); they are listed as missing days and never filled with zero or estimated.

tables.name: swaps_daily
tables.purpose: success_swaps = swaps with status SUCCESS per created_day (UTC); median_usd = the median amount_in_usd of successful swaps with a known USD value (ClickHouse quantileExact(0.5): the value at index floor(n/2) of the sorted amounts). Days whose swaps are marked partial in source_coverage (provider near-explorer, dataset intents_swaps: 2025-11-09 oldest edge, 2026-01-27/28/30 quarantined pages, 2026-04-02 to 2026-04-23 explorer cursor jump, 2026-07-23 quarantined page) are left out of this series entirely, and so are the two days (2026-02-02 and 2026-02-04) on which a successful swap has no USD value (the day is incomplete by the research definition); they are listed as missing days and never filled with zero or estimated.

tables.name: intents_mix_daily
tables.purpose: Volume = successful swaps with a known USD value (the F4 definition), per created_day (UTC). Each swap leg (origin_asset, destination_asset) is joined to nearesis_live.asset_registry on provider_asset_id. F5 stable_share: both legs are a stablecoin, by upper-cased registry symbol_observed in {DAI, FRAX, USD1, USDC, USDCX, USDG, USDT, USDT0, USDe, USDf} (the frozen research snapshot's stablecoinSet; USDT0 and USDCx variants count, a deprecated-suffix symbol does not). F6 no_near_share: both legs mapped and NEITHER leg has registry blockchain 'near' (a stablecoin or token issued on NEAR counts as a NEAR-chain asset). F7 near_token_share: either leg has symbol NEAR or wNEAR (asset ids listed in asset_sets: nep141:wrap.near is wNEAR on NEAR; the NEAR token on BNB chain is also listed; F6 and F7 can overlap only for that BNB-chain leg). unknown_share: a swap with an unmapped leg (no registry row) is counted in unknown_usd only, never in F5, F6 or F7; shares divide by total_usd including unknown. The registry rows are used regardless of valid_from: every row has valid_from 2026-05-01 (the registry load stamp, valid_to is null everywhere), and applying it as a validity start would wrongly unmap every swap before that date. Shares are the share of the day's USD volume, not of swap counts. Days whose swaps are marked partial in source_coverage (provider near-explorer, dataset intents_swaps: 2025-11-09 oldest edge, 2026-01-27/28/30 quarantined pages, 2026-04-02 to 2026-04-23 explorer cursor jump, 2026-07-23 quarantined page) are left out of this series entirely, and so are the two days (2026-02-02 and 2026-02-04) on which a successful swap has no USD value (the day is incomplete by the research definition); they are listed as missing days and never filled with zero or estimated.

tables.name: chain_pairs_monthly
tables.purpose: USD volume (successful, known-USD swaps, same definition as F4, complete days only) by calendar month (m = first day of the month) and registry blockchain of the origin and destination asset; the ten pairs with the largest volume over the whole window are listed, each with the months where it has volume. 2025-11 starts on 2025-11-10 and 2026-11 ends on 2026-11-13: those two months are partial.

tables.name: excursion_routes
tables.purpose: The ten routes (origin asset to destination asset) with the most USD volume among successful known-USD swaps that have a NEAR or wNEAR leg, over 2026-05-22 to 2026-05-27, the days on which the near_token_share series peaks. Used only to explain that excursion.

tables.name: asset_sets
tables.purpose: Every registry row whose upper-cased symbol is in the stablecoin set {DAI, FRAX, USD1, USDC, USDCX, USDG, USDT, USDT0, USDe, USDf} (set_name stable) or is NEAR / wNEAR (set_name near_token).

tables.name: head_accounts_break
tables.purpose: The 12 head accounts (organic transactions >= 100 on a day) with the largest of their before and after totals. Before = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-01 and after = 2026-04-02 to 2026-05-02, 31 days each. tx_* sums organic transactions on the days the account was in the head; avg_daily_* = that sum divided by 31. On a day below 100 organic transactions the account is not stored, so the averages are lower bounds for accounts that were in the head on fewer days than 31 (head_days_* says how many).

tables.name: near_price_daily
tables.purpose: The provider's last price sample of the UTC day (close_raw as received, exact string). The free plan has no daily OHLC history, so the day's candle is built from 24 hourly samples.

tables.name: swaps_coverage
tables.purpose: One row per day (2025-11-09 to the last day) on which the Explorer swap fetch is not complete. These days are excluded from every swap series (F4 to F8) and listed, never filled.

tables.name: fees/fees_total_daily
tables.purpose: Per UTC block day: the sum of tokens_burnt (yoctoNEAR, and the same in NEAR = yocto / 10^24) and gas_burnt over every row of execution_outcomes (transaction outcomes and receipt outcomes, incl. refund receipts that burn no tokens), the outcome count, and the day's mean gas price = sum of blocks.gas_price / block count. Gross tokens_burnt of the outcomes. Whether part of a fee is burnt or paid to the called contract: nearcore docs state a 30% contract reward up to protocol version 86 and 0% from 87 (docs/economics/SEMANTICS.md); the mainnet activation date of version 87 is not verified here, so no burnt/paid split is applied.

tables.name: fees/fees_intents_daily
tables.purpose: Gross tokens_burnt and gas_burnt of execution outcomes whose executor_account_id is in the narrow set (core Intents contracts: intents.near) or the wide set (core plus the settlement footprint: bridge-refuel.hot.tg, intents.near). The wide set rule: an account discovered among the executors of receipts originating from transactions sent to intents.near, carrying at least 0.5% of that Intents-origin burn and getting at least 50% of its own burn from it. Gross tokens_burnt of the outcomes. Whether part of a fee is burnt or paid to the called contract: nearcore docs state a 30% contract reward up to protocol version 86 and 0% from 87 (docs/economics/SEMANTICS.md); the mainnet activation date of version 87 is not verified here, so no burnt/paid split is applied.

tables.name: fees/fees_by_receiver_top
tables.purpose: For scope "window" and each calendar quarter present: accounts ranked by the sum of tokens_burnt over the outcomes they executed (executor_account_id: a contract for receipt outcomes, the signer for transaction outcomes, so a user or bot account appears for the conversion burn of its own transactions). share_of_total_pct = account tokens / all tokens burnt on the covered days of the scope. Quarters: Q4 2025 starts 2025-11-10, Q4 2026 ends 2026-11-13. Gross tokens_burnt of the outcomes. Whether part of a fee is burnt or paid to the called contract: nearcore docs state a 30% contract reward up to protocol version 86 and 0% from 87 (docs/economics/SEMANTICS.md); the mainnet activation date of version 87 is not verified here, so no burnt/paid split is applied.

tables.name: fees/tx_fee_intents_daily
tables.purpose: Transactions per UTC day whose receiver is a narrow (intents.near) or wide (bridge-refuel.hot.tg, intents.near) account, with the transaction-level fee the dataset carries: receipt_conversion_* = gas and tokens burnt converting the signed transaction into its first receipt (transaction day). Reconciliation to fees_intents_daily on days where both exist: narrow_outcomes_per_tx = receipt outcomes executed on the narrow contracts / transactions sent to them; narrow_direct_toll = executor tokens of the narrow contracts + conversion tokens of transactions sent to them.

tables.name: fees/fees_take_rate_gas_daily
tables.purpose: take_rate_gas_bps = (NEAR burnt by the Intents contracts that day x that day's NEAR/USD close) / (that day's Intents successful known-USD volume) x 10^4, in basis points of settled value, for the narrow and the wide set. The 30 day figure is the ratio of sums over the trailing 30 calendar days (days with burn, price and volume all present; null below 15 such days). intents_share_of_burn_pct = Intents burn / all NEAR burnt that day. This is the gas/burn toll only: protocol-level burn of outcomes executed on the Intents contracts. Not verified here: which share of a fee is burnt versus paid to the called contract under current protocol rules (documented 30% to the contract up to protocol version 86, 0% from 87, activation date unverified).

tables.name: fees/fees_footprint_discovery
tables.purpose: Top 40 executor accounts by tokens burnt per sample day among receipt outcomes belonging to transactions whose receiver is intents.near (same-day receipts), summed over the sample days. Intents-origin total over all executors: 224742573293700554423025664 yocto (the top-40 sum is 222851175396096106185375744 yocto). dependence_pct = the account's Intents-origin burn / its own total burn on the same days. Core set: intents.near. Wide set: bridge-refuel.hot.tg, intents.near.

tables.name: fees/toll_daily
tables.purpose: spread = USD in minus USD out of successful swaps with both marks, volume-weighted in basis points of input, per route group (all routes; both legs USD stablecoins); app fees = the integrator appFees on each successful swap (input USD x fee bps / 10000), and app_fee_bps = app fee USD / successful input USD x 10000.
